title: Act I
originalSetting: Das Theater ist eine felsige Gegend, hier und da mit Bäumen überwachsen; auf beiden Seiten sind gangbare Berge, nebst einem runden Tempel.
setting: A rocky landscape, overgrown here and there with trees; passable mountains on both sides, beside a round temple.

scenes.title: Zu Hilfe! Zu Hilfe! (Introduktion)
scenes.originalDescription: Tamino im prächtigen Jagdkleide eilt von einem Felsen herunter, eine Schlange verfolgt ihn. Drei verschleierte Damen der Königin der Nacht erscheinen und töten das Ungeheuer.
scenes.description: Prince Tamino rushes down from the rocks in magnificent hunting attire, pursued by a giant serpent. He collapses in a faint, whereupon Three Ladies of the Queen of the Night appear and slay the monster.

lines.original: Zu Hilfe! Zu Hilfe! sonst bin ich verloren,
lines.literal: To help! To help! Otherwise am I lost,

tokens.notes: Idiomatic cry for help; dative of purpose with 'zu'.

lines.grammarNote: V2 word order triggered by the initial adverb 'sonst' (sonst bin ich...).

lines.original: der listigen Schlange zum Opfer erkoren –
lines.literal: to the cunning serpent as a sacrifice chosen –

tokens.notes: Dative singular feminine with weak adjective ending '-en'.
Archaic past participle of erkiesen (to choose/destine).

lines.original: barmherzige Götter! Schon nahet sie sich,
lines.literal: merciful gods! Already nears it itself,
lines.grammarNote: Inversion after adverb 'schon': verb 'nahet' precedes subject 'sie'.

lines.original: ach rettet mich, ach rettet, schützet mich!
lines.literal: ah save me, ah save, protect me!

cues.speaker: Tamino
cues.stageDirection: Er fällt in Ohnmacht; sogleich öffnet sich die Pforte des Tempels; drei verschleierte Damen kommen heraus, jede mit einem silbernen Wurfspieß.
cues.stageDirectionTranslation: He collapses in a faint; at once the temple gates open; three veiled ladies emerge, each bearing a silver lance.

lines.literal: Die, monster, through our might!
Triumph! Triumph! It is accomplished

tokens.notes: Inseparable prefix verb voll-bringen; past participle.

lines.literal: the heroic deed! He is freed
through our arm's bravery.
lines.grammarNote: Genitive construction: 'uns'res Armes Tapferkeit' = the bravery of our arm.

lines.original: Ein holder Jüngling, sanft und schön!
lines.literal: A lovely youth, gentle and handsome!

lines.original: So schön, als ich noch nie geseh'n.
lines.literal: So handsome, as I yet never have seen.
lines.grammarNote: Ellipsis of auxiliary verb 'habe' in subordinate clause.

lines.original: Ja, ja, gewiß! zum Malen schön.
lines.literal: Yes, yes, certainly! for painting handsome.

lines.original: Würd' ich mein Herz der Liebe weih'n,
lines.literal: Would I my heart to love consecrate,

tokens.notes: Conditional inversion: 'Würde ich' = If I were to...

lines.grammarNote: Conditional clause introduced without 'wenn', using verb-first inversion ('Würd' ich...').

lines.original: so müßt' es dieser Jüngling sein.
lines.literal: so must it this youth be.

lines.literal: Let us to our princess hurry,
to-her this news to impart.
lines.grammarNote: Infinitive clause with 'zu erteilen' taking dative 'ihr' and accusative 'diese Nachricht'.

lines.literal: Perhaps that this handsome man,

lines.literal: the former peace to-her give can.

tokens.notes: Verb-final in subordinate clause introduced by 'daß'.

lines.grammarNote: Subordinate clause word order: finite verb 'kann' placed at the very end.

lines.original: So geht und sagt es ihr,
lines.literal: So go and say it to-her,
I remain meanwhile here. –

lines.original: Nein, nein, geht ihr nur hin,
lines.literal: No, no, go you just thither,
I watch here for him!

lines.original: Nein, nein, das kann nicht sein,
lines.literal: No, no, that can not be,
I protect him alone!
I remain meanwhile here ...
I watch here for him ...
I protect him alone ...
... I remain ...
... I watch ...
... I protect ...

lines.original: Ich sollte fort! Ei, ei! wie fein!
lines.literal: I ought away! Well, well! How fine!

tokens.notes: Modal 'sollen' with directional adverb 'fort' acting as verb.

lines.original: Sie wären gern bei ihm allein.
lines.literal: They would-be gladly with him alone.

tokens.meaning: would gladly be / would like to be

lines.original: Nein, nein, das kann nicht sein!
lines.literal: No, no, that cannot be!

lines.original: Was sollte ich darum nicht geben,
lines.literal: What should I for-that not give,
lines.grammarNote: Rhetorical question: 'What would I not give for that...'

lines.original: könnt' ich mit diesem Jüngling leben!
lines.literal: could I with this youth live!
lines.grammarNote: Optative conditional inversion ('könnt' ich...').

lines.literal: Had I him only so completely alone!

tokens.meaning: had I / if only I had

lines.grammarNote: Optative wish with 'doch': 'Hätt' ich ihn doch...' = If only I had him...

lines.original: Doch keine geht, es kann nicht sein.
lines.literal: Yet none goes, it cannot be.

lines.original: Am besten ist es nun, ich geh'.
lines.literal: At best is it now, [that] I go.
You youth handsome and loving,
you beloved youth, fare well,
until I you see-again.

tokens.meaning: see again (separable prefix verb in subordinate clause)

lines.grammarNote: Separable verb prefix 'wieder-' stays attached to verb stem at end of subordinate clause.

scenes.title: Der Vogelfänger bin ich ja (Lied)
scenes.originalDescription: Papageno kommt einen Fußsteig herunter mit einer großen Vogelsteige auf dem Rücken und einer fünftönigen Panflöte in der Hand.
scenes.description: Papageno, bird-catcher to the Queen of the Night, arrives playing his panpipes and singing joyfully of his carefree life catching birds and wishing for a wife.

lines.literal: The bird-catcher am I indeed –
lines.grammarNote: Topicalized predicate noun ('Der Vogelfänger') triggers subject-verb inversion ('bin ich').

lines.literal: always merry, hurrah, hopsasa!
I bird-catcher am known

lines.original: bei Alt und Jung im ganzen Land.
lines.literal: to old and young in-the whole land.
[I] know with the luring [how] to deal
lines.grammarNote: Infinitive construction with separable prefix: 'um-zu-gehen'.

lines.literal: and myself on piping to understand!
lines.grammarNote: Reflexive idiom: 'sich auf etwas (Akk.) verstehen' = to be an expert in something.

lines.literal: Therefore can I glad and merry be,
lines.grammarNote: Inversion after causal conjunction 'drum' (darum).

lines.literal: for all birds are indeed mine.

I bird-catcher am known

lines.literal: to old and young in-the whole land.

lines.literal: A net for maidens would-like I,
lines.grammarNote: Object topicalization ('Ein Netz...') causing verb-second inversion ('möchte ich').

lines.literal: I would-catch them by-the-dozen for myself.

lines.literal: Then would-lock I them at my-place in,

tokens.meaning: at my house / in my dwelling

lines.grammarNote: Separable verb prefix 'ein' at the clause bracket end.

lines.literal: and all maidens would-be mine.
If all maidens would-be mine,

lines.literal: so would-trade I dutifully sugar in:

lines.literal: she, who to-me dearest would-be,
lines.grammarNote: Dative of interest ('mir am liebsten').

lines.original: der gäb' ich gleich den Zucker her.
lines.literal: to-her would-give I at-once the sugar forth.

tokens.meaning: would hand over / give forth (subjunctive II)

lines.original: Und küßte sie mich zärtlich dann,
lines.literal: And kissed she me tenderly then,

tokens.meaning: kissed / were to kiss (subjunctive conditional inversion)

lines.grammarNote: Hypothetical condition expressed through verb-initial syntax ('küßte sie mich...').

lines.literal: would-be she my wife and I her husband.

lines.original: Sie schlief' an meiner Seite ein,
lines.literal: She would-fall-asleep at my side in,

tokens.meaning: would fall asleep (separable verb in subjunctive II)

lines.original: ich wiegte wie ein Kind sie ein.
lines.literal: I would-rock like a child her in [to sleep].

scenes.title: Dies Bildnis ist bezaubernd schön (Arie)
scenes.originalDescription: Tamino betrachtet das Bildnis Paminas, das ihm die drei Damen übergeben haben.
scenes.description: Tamino gazes upon the portrait of Pamina given to him by the Three Ladies and is overcome by a profound and overwhelming love.

lines.literal: This portrait is enchantingly beautiful,

lines.original: wie noch kein Auge je geseh'n.
lines.literal: as yet no eye ever has seen.

lines.original: Ich fühl' es, wie dies Götterbild
lines.literal: I feel it, how this divine-image

tokens.meaning: image of a goddess / divine portrait

lines.original: mein Herz mit neuer Regung füllt.
lines.literal: my heart with new emotion fills.
lines.grammarNote: Verb-final in subordinate clause introduced by 'wie'.

lines.original: Dies Etwas kann ich zwar nicht nennen,
lines.literal: This something can I admittedly not name,
lines.grammarNote: Topicalized direct object ('Dies Etwas') causing V2 inversion ('kann ich').

lines.original: doch fühl' ich's hier wie Feuer brennen;
lines.literal: yet feel I it here like fire burn;

tokens.meaning: feel I it (contraction: fühle ich es)

lines.literal: shall the feeling love be?
lines.grammarNote: Verb-first question syntax ('soll die Empfindung...').

lines.original: Ja, ja, die Liebe ist's allein.
lines.literal: Yes, yes, love is it alone.

lines.original: O wenn ich sie nur finden könnte!
lines.literal: O if I her only find could!
lines.grammarNote: Unfulfilled wish clause with 'wenn' and subjunctive II 'könnte' at clause end.

lines.original: O wenn sie doch schon vor mir stünde!
lines.literal: O if she only already before me stood!

tokens.meaning: stood / were standing (subjunctive II of stehen)

lines.grammarNote: Subjunctive II form 'stünde' expresses an ardent hypothetical wish.

lines.original: Ich würde – würde – warm und rein –
lines.literal: I would – would – warm and pure –
what would I?
I would her full of rapture

lines.grammarNote: Preposition 'an' + accusative indicating movement towards the body.

lines.original: und ewig wäre sie dann mein!
lines.literal: and forever would-be she then mine!

scenes.title: O zitt're nicht, mein lieber Sohn (Rezitativ und Arie)
scenes.titleTranslation: O tremble not, my dear son (Recitative and Aria)
scenes.originalDescription: Die Berge teilen sich unter heftigem Donner auseinander, und die Königin auf ihrem sternenverzierten Thron wird sichtbar.
scenes.description: Under heavy thunder and lightning, the mountains part to reveal the Queen of the Night on a starry throne. She laments the kidnapping of her daughter Pamina by Sarastro and charges Tamino with her rescue.

lines.original: O zitt're nicht, mein lieber Sohn,
lines.literal: O tremble not, my dear son,
you are innocent, wise, pious –

lines.original: Ein Jüngling so wie du, vermag am besten,
lines.literal: A youth such as you, is-able at best,
the deeply-afflicted mother's-heart to console. –
lines.grammarNote: Infinitive construction completing 'vermag am besten'.

lines.literal: For suffering am I chosen,
lines.grammarNote: Topicalized prepositional phrase ('Zum Leiden') triggers inversion ('bin ich').

lines.literal: for my daughter is-missing to-me.

tokens.notes: German construction: 'jemandem fehlen' = to be missed by someone.

lines.grammarNote: German idiom: 'sie fehlt mir' = I miss her (literally: she is lacking to me).

lines.original: Durch sie ging all mein Glück verloren,
lines.literal: Through her went all my happiness lost,
lines.grammarNote: Idiom: 'verlorengehen' (to get lost / be destroyed).

lines.literal: a villain fled away with her.
Still see I her trembling
with fearful shuddering,
her anxious quivering,
her timid struggling.

lines.original: Ich mußte sie mir rauben sehen,
lines.literal: I had-to her from-me robbed see,

tokens.meaning: see her being stolen from me

lines.grammarNote: Dativus ethicus / separationis: 'mir rauben' = to rob away from me.

lines.original: ach helft!, war alles was sie sprach –
lines.literal: ah help!, was all that she spoke –
yet in vain was her pleading,

lines.original: denn meine Hilfe war zu schwach.
lines.literal: for my help was too weak.

lines.original: Du wirst sie zu befreien gehen,
lines.literal: You will her to liberate go,
lines.grammarNote: Future tense 'wirst ... gehen' governing the final infinitive 'zu befreien'.

lines.original: du wirst der Tochter Retter sein.
lines.literal: you will the daughter's savior be.
lines.grammarNote: Pre-nominal genitive 'der Tochter Retter' = the savior of my daughter.

lines.original: Und werd' ich dich als Sieger sehen,
lines.literal: And will I you as victor see,

tokens.meaning: shall I / if I shall (conditional inversion)

lines.grammarNote: Verb-first conditional inversion ('werd' ich dich... sehen' = and if I see you as victor).

lines.original: so sei sie dann auf ewig dein.
lines.literal: so be she then for eternity yours.
lines.grammarNote: Subjunctive I 'sei' used in third-person imperative / promissory sense ('so let her be yours').

scenes.title: Hm! hm! hm! hm! (Quintett)
scenes.originalDescription: Papageno hat ein goldenes Schloß vor dem Mund. Die drei Damen befreien ihn und bringen Tamino die Zauberflöte und Papageno das Glockenspiel.
scenes.description: Papageno laments his punishment for lying with a padlock on his mouth. The Three Ladies unlock it, cautioning against dishonesty, and bestow upon Tamino the magic flute and upon Papageno a magical chime of silver bells.

cues.speaker: Papageno
cues.stageDirection: deutet traurig auf sein Schloß am Mund
cues.stageDirectionTranslation: points sadly to the padlock on his mouth

lines.literal: Hm! hm! hm! hm!

lines.original: Der Arme kann von Strafe sagen,
lines.literal: The poor [man] can of punishment speak,

tokens.meaning: to speak of / testify to punishment

lines.literal: for his speech is gone!
Hm! hm! hm! hm!

lines.original: Ich kann nichts tun, als dich beklagen,
lines.literal: I can nothing do, but you pity,

lines.original: weil ich zu schwach zu helfen bin!
lines.literal: because I too weak to help am!
lines.grammarNote: Subordinate clause word order: finite verb 'bin' placed at the end after 'zu helfen'.

lines.literal: The Queen pardons you,

lines.literal: remits the punishment to-you through me. –

cues.speaker: First Lady
cues.stageDirection: nimmt ihm das Schloß vom Mund weg
cues.stageDirectionTranslation: removes the padlock from his mouth

lines.literal: Now chatters Papageno again!

the mournful [man] will joyful be,
the confirmed-bachelor takes love in [captivates].

scenes.title: Du feines Täubchen, nur herein (Terzett)
scenes.originalDescription: Ein prächtiges Zimmer im Palast Sarastros. Monostatos und Sklaven führen Pamina herein.
scenes.description: In Sarastro's palace, the overseer Monostatos threatens Pamina, but when Papageno wanders in, both Monostatos and Papageno terrify each other believing the other to be the devil.

lines.literal: You delicate little-dove, just [come] in.

tokens.meaning: just come in (directional adverb as command)

lines.grammarNote: Directional adverb 'herein' used elliptically as an imperative motion verb.

lines.literal: O what torment, what agony!
Forfeited is your life.
lines.grammarNote: Fronted predicate adjective causing inversion: 'Verloren ist dein Leben'.

lines.original: Der Tod macht mich nicht beben;
lines.literal: Death makes me not tremble;
lines.grammarNote: Causative 'machen' + bare infinitive: 'macht mich nicht beben'.

lines.literal: only my mother grieves me,

tokens.meaning: causes me grief / makes me feel sorrow
tokens.notes: Archaic/idiomatic: 'jemanden dauern' = to move someone to pity/sorrow.

lines.grammarNote: Idiomatic construction: 'jemanden dauern' = to make someone feel sorrow.

lines.original: sie stirbt vor Gram ganz sicherlich.
lines.literal: she dies from grief completely surely.
lines.grammarNote: Preposition 'vor' expressing involuntary cause or emotion (vor Gram, vor Freude).

lines.literal: Hey, slaves, put on-her fetters on;

lines.literal: because nothing, barbarian! you move can.
lines.grammarNote: Verb-final in causal clause with 'weil': 'dich rühren kann'.

cues.speaker: Pamina
cues.stageDirection: sinkt in Ohnmacht auf ein Sofa

cues.stageDirection: Die Sklaven gehen ab. Papageno am Fenster von außen, ohne gleich gesehen zu werden.

lines.original: Wo bin ich wohl?! wo mag ich sein?
lines.literal: Where am I perhaps?! Where may I be?

lines.original: Aha, da find' ich Leute, gewagt; ich geh' hinein.
lines.literal: Aha, there find I people; ventured [it]; I go inside.
Beautiful maiden young and pure,
much whiter still than chalk...

cues.speaker: Papageno
cues.stageDirection: Monostatos und Papageno sehen sich, – erschrickt einer über den andern.
cues.stageDirectionTranslation: Monostatos and Papageno see each other, – each terrified of the other.

lines.original: Hu – – das ist – der Teufel sicherlich.
lines.literal: Hu – – that is – the devil surely.

lines.original: Hab Mitleid – verschone mich – Hu – Hu –
lines.literal: Have pity – spare me – Hu – Hu –

scenes.title: Bei Männern, welche Liebe fühlen (Duett)
scenes.originalDescription: Pamina und Papageno besingen die erhabene Kraft der Liebe zwischen Mann und Frau.
scenes.description: Pamina and Papageno reflect on the divine sacredness of love and harmonious matrimony before setting off to find Tamino.

lines.literal: In men, who love feel,
lines.grammarNote: Relative clause: verb 'fühlen' at end.

lines.original: fehlt auch ein gutes Herze nicht.
lines.literal: lacks also a good heart not [is a good heart not lacking].
lines.grammarNote: Archaic noun form 'Herze' for standard modern 'Herz'.

lines.literal: The sweet impulses to-feel-with [sympathize],

tokens.meaning: to sympathize / feel in common (separable infinitive)

lines.original: ist dann der Weiber erste Pflicht.
lines.literal: is then the women's first duty.
lines.grammarNote: Pre-nominal genitive 'der Weiber erste Pflicht'.

lines.original: Wir wollen uns der Liebe freu'n,
lines.literal: We will ourselves in-the love rejoice,

tokens.meaning: in love (genitive of object of rejoicing)

lines.grammarNote: Genitive object with reflexive verb: 'sich einer Sache (Gen.) freuen'.

lines.original: wir leben durch die Lieb' allein.
lines.literal: we live through love alone.

to-her sacrifices every creature.
lines.grammarNote: Inversion after fronted dative pronoun 'ihr' (to love).

lines.literal: She spices our days-of-life,

lines.original: sie wirkt im Kreise der Natur.
lines.literal: she works in-the cycle of nature.

lines.original: Ihr hoher Zweck zeigt deutlich an:
lines.literal: Her elevated purpose indicates clearly on:

lines.original: nichts Edler's sei, als Weib und Mann.
lines.literal: nothing nobler be, than wife and husband [woman and man].
lines.grammarNote: Subjunctive I 'sei' used in reported evaluation ('that nothing is nobler...').

lines.original: Mann und Weib, und Weib und Mann,
lines.literal: Husband and wife, and wife and husband,
reach unto the godhead up-to.
lines.grammarNote: Separable verb 'anreichen an' = to touch / reach up to divinity.

scenes.title: Zum Ziele führt dich diese Bahn (Finale I)
scenes.titleTranslation: To the goal leads you this path (Finale I)
scenes.originalDescription: Ein heiliger Hain vor drei Pforten: der Weisheit, der Vernunft und der Natur. Sarastros Tempelbezirk.
scenes.description: The Three Boys guide Tamino to the gates of Sarastro's sanctuary. Tamino converses with the Speaker of the Temple, learns that Sarastro is an enlightened priest rather than a tyrant, plays his flute to tame wild beasts, and is reunited with Pamina before Sarastro's triumphal procession.

lines.original: Zum Ziele führt dich diese Bahn,
lines.literal: To-the goal leads you this path,
lines.grammarNote: Fronted prepositional phrase 'Zum Ziele' triggers V2 inversion ('führt dich diese Bahn').

lines.original: doch mußt du Jüngling männlich siegen,
lines.literal: yet must you youth manfully conquer,
therefore listen our teaching to [heed our instruction]:
Be steadfast, patient, and discreet! –
lines.grammarNote: The three Masonic virtues demanded of initiates: steadfastness, patience, discretion.

lines.original: Ihr holden Knaben sagt mir an,
lines.literal: You gracious boys tell to-me on [tell me],
whether I Pamina rescue can? –
lines.grammarNote: Subordinate clause word order: modal verb 'kann' placed at the very end.

lines.original: Dies kund zu tun steht uns nicht an;
lines.literal: This known to make stands to-us not on [is not fitting for us to disclose];

tokens.meaning: to make known / disclose (separable infinitive with zu)
to be fitting / be incumbent upon (governs dative 'uns')

lines.grammarNote: Idiomatic construction: 'jemandem anstehen' = to be proper/fitting for someone.

lines.literal: be steadfast, patient and discreet!

lines.original: Bedenke dies, kurz: sei ein Mann. –
lines.literal: Consider this, in short: be a man. –

lines.original: Dann Jüngling wirst du männlich siegen.
lines.literal: Then youth will you manfully triumph.
The wisdom-teaching of-these boys

tokens.meaning: of these boys (genitive plural weak noun ending -n)

lines.original: sei ewig mir ins Herz gegraben.
lines.literal: be forever to-me into-the heart engraved.
lines.grammarNote: Subjunctive I 'sei' used optatively: 'may it be engraved into my heart forever'.

lines.original: Wo bin ich nun? – Was wird mit mir?
lines.literal: Where am I now? – What becomes with me [what will become of me]?

lines.original: Ist dies der Sitz der Götter hier? –
lines.literal: Is this the seat of-the gods here? –

lines.original: Es zeigen die Pforten – es zeigen die Säulen,
lines.literal: It show the portals – it show the columns [the gates and columns show],
lines.grammarNote: Expletive 'es' anticipatory subject: 'Es zeigen die Pforten' = The portals show.

lines.original: daß Klugheit, und Arbeit, und Künste hier weilen.
lines.literal: that prudence, and labor, and arts here dwell.
lines.grammarNote: Enlightenment triad: Prudence, Industry, and the Arts.

lines.original: Wo Tätigkeit thronet und Müßiggang weicht,
lines.literal: Where activity thrones and idleness yields,

lines.original: erhält seine Herrschaft das Laster nicht leicht.
lines.literal: maintains its dominion vice not easily.
lines.grammarNote: OVS inversion: object 'seine Herrschaft' precedes subject 'das Laster'.

lines.original: Ich wage mich mutig zur Pforte hinein.
lines.literal: I venture myself boldly to-the portal inside.

lines.original: Die Absicht ist edel, und lauter, und rein.
lines.literal: The intention is noble, and sincere, and pure.
Tremble, cowardly villain!

tokens.meaning: tremble / shudder (imperative singular with inchoative prefix er-)

lines.literal: Pamina to-rescue is to-me duty!
lines.grammarNote: Classical -en accusative suffix for feminine proper names (Paminen).

cues.speaker: Tamino
cues.stageDirection: geht an die Pforte rechts, macht sie auf, und als er hinein will, hört man von fern eine Stimme
cues.stageDirectionTranslation: goes to the portal on the right, opens it, and as he tries to enter, a voice is heard from afar

lines.literal: Back!

lines.original: Zurück? zurück? – so wag ich hier mein Glück!
lines.literal: Back? Back? – so venture I here my luck!

cues.speaker: Tamino
cues.stageDirectionTranslation: goes to the portal on the left

lines.literal: Back!
Also here calls one "back"?

lines.original: Da seh' ich noch eine Tür.
lines.literal: There see I yet another door.

lines.original: Vielleicht find' ich den Eingang hier!
lines.literal: Perhaps find I the entrance here!

cues.speaker: Tamino
cues.stageDirection: Er klopft, ein alter Priester erscheint.
cues.stageDirectionTranslation: He knocks, an old priest appears.

lines.original: Wo willst du kühner Fremdling hin?
lines.literal: Where want you bold stranger thither [where do you intend to go]?
lines.grammarNote: Modal 'wollen' + directional adverb 'hin' implying a verb of motion.

lines.original: Was suchst du hier im Heiligtum? –
lines.literal: What seek you here in-the sanctuary? –

tokens.meaning: seek you / are you looking for

lines.literal: Of love and virtue [the] property.

lines.original: Die Worte sind von hohem Sinn –
lines.literal: The words are of high meaning [profound import] –

tokens.meaning: of lofty meaning / high sense (dative masculine)

lines.original: allein, wie willst du diese finden?
lines.literal: yet, how will you these find?

lines.original: Dich leitet Lieb' und Tugend nicht,
lines.literal: You guides love and virtue not [love and virtue do not guide you],
lines.grammarNote: OSV word order: direct object 'Dich' is placed first for emphasis.

lines.original: weil Tod und Rache dich entzünden.
lines.literal: because death and vengeance you inflame.
lines.grammarNote: Subordinate clause word order: verb 'entzünden' at the end.

lines.literal: Only revenge for the villain.

lines.original: Den wirst du wohl bei uns nicht finden.
lines.literal: That-one will you surely among us not find.
Sarastro rules in these grounds [territories]?
Yes, yes, Sarastro rules here.

lines.original: Doch in der Weisheit Tempel nicht? –
lines.literal: Yet in wisdom's temple not? –
He rules in-the temple of wisdom here! –
So is then everything hypocrisy! –
Want you already again to-go [do you want to leave already]?

lines.original: Ja ich will gehen, froh, und frei –
lines.literal: Yes I will go, glad, and free –
never your temple see! –
Explain yourself more-closely to-me,
you deceives a deception [a fraud is deceiving you]! –
lines.grammarNote: OVS word order: accusative pronoun 'dich' precedes verb and subject 'ein Betrug'.

lines.literal: Sarastro dwells here,
that is to-me already enough! –

lines.original: Wenn du dein Leben liebst, so rede, bleibe da! –
lines.literal: If you your life love, so speak, stay there! –
Sarastro hate you [do you hate Sarastro]?
lines.grammarNote: Fronted object 'Sarastro' in a question: 'Do you hate Sarastro?'

lines.literal: I hate him eternally, yes! –

lines.original: So gib mir deine Gründe an! –
lines.literal: So give to-me your reasons on [state your reasons]! –

lines.original: Er ist ein Unmensch, ein Tyrann! –
lines.literal: He is a monster [inhuman being], a tyrant! –

lines.original: Ist das, was du gesagt, erwiesen?
lines.literal: Is that, which you said, proven?
lines.grammarNote: Ellipsis of auxiliary 'hast' in relative clause ('was du gesagt [hast]').

lines.literal: Through an unhappy woman proven,
whom grief and misery oppresses down!

tokens.meaning: whom / which (relative pronoun referring to Weib)

lines.grammarNote: Relative pronoun 'das' takes neuter gender from grammatical antecedent 'Weib'.

lines.original: Ein Weib hat also dich berückt? –
lines.literal: A woman has thus you bewitched [deluded]? –

lines.original: Ein Weib tut wenig, plaudert viel,
lines.literal: A woman does little, chatters much,
you youth believe the tongue-play [idle gossip]? –
lines.grammarNote: 'Glauben' governs the dative of the thing believed ('dem Zungenspiel').

lines.literal: O laid only Sarastro to-you

tokens.meaning: would set forth / explain (subjunctive II inversion)

lines.grammarNote: Optative wish with 'doch': 'O legte doch Sarastro dir... für' = If only Sarastro explained to you...

lines.literal: the intention of-his action before [explained his action to you]. –

lines.original: Die Absicht ist nur allzu klar!
lines.literal: The intention is only all-too clear!

lines.original: Riß nicht der Räuber ohn' Erbarmen
lines.literal: Tore not the robber without mercy
Pamina out of-the mother's arms? –

lines.original: Ja Jüngling, was du sagst, ist wahr! –
lines.literal: Yes youth, what you say, is true! –

lines.original: Wo ist sie, die er uns geraubt?
lines.literal: Where is she, whom he from-us robbed?

tokens.meaning: robbed / abducted (past participle with ellipsis of 'hat')

lines.grammarNote: Dativus separationis: 'uns geraubt' = stolen from us.

lines.literal: One sacrificed perhaps her already [has she already been sacrificed]? –

lines.original: Dir dies zu sagen, teurer Sohn,
lines.literal: To-you this to say, dear son,

lines.original: ist jetzt und mir noch nicht erlaubt. –
lines.literal: is now and to-me not yet permitted. –
lines.grammarNote: Impersonal passive with dative: 'mir ist nicht erlaubt' = I am not permitted.

lines.original: Erklär dies Rätsel, täusch mich nicht!
lines.literal: Explain this riddle, deceive me not!

lines.original: Die Zunge bindet Eid und Pflicht!
lines.literal: The tongue binds oath and duty [oath and duty bind the tongue]!
lines.grammarNote: OVS word order: 'Die Zunge' is accusative, subject 'Eid und Pflicht' follows.

lines.original: Wann also wird die Decke schwinden? –
lines.literal: When thus will the veil vanish [when will the veil be lifted]? –

lines.original: Sobald dich führt der Freundschaft Hand
lines.literal: As soon as you leads of-friendship hand [friendship's hand leads you]
lines.grammarNote: Inversion in subordinate clause: object 'dich' precedes verb and subject 'der Freundschaft Hand'.

lines.literal: into-the sanctuary to-the eternal bond.

lines.original: O ew'ge Nacht! Wann wirst du schwinden?
lines.literal: O eternal night! When will you vanish?

lines.original: Wann wird das Licht mein Auge finden? –
lines.literal: When will the light my eye find?
Soon, youth, or never!
Soon, say you, or never? –
You invisible-ones tell to-me:
lives then Pamina still [is Pamina still alive]?
lines.grammarNote: Verb-first question syntax.

lines.literal: Pamina lives still!
She lives, she lives!
I thank you for-that.
lines.grammarNote: 'Danken' governs the dative person ('euch').

lines.original: O wenn ich doch im Stande wäre,
lines.literal: O if I only in-the position were [were able],

tokens.meaning: were capable / in a position to (subjunctive II of sein)

lines.grammarNote: Idiom: 'imstande sein' = to be able/capable.

lines.literal: Almighty-ones, to your honor,
with every tone my gratitude
to portray, as it here,
here sprang forth.

cues.speaker: Tamino
cues.stageDirection: Er spielt. Es kommen wilde Tiere von allen Arten hervor, ihm zuzuhören. Er hört auf, und sie fliehen. Die Vögel pfeifen dazu.
cues.stageDirectionTranslation: He plays. Wild beasts of all kinds emerge to listen to him. When he stops, they flee. Birds chirp along.

lines.original: Wie stark ist nicht dein Zauberton,
lines.literal: How strong is not your magic-tone [how potent is your magical sound],
lines.grammarNote: Exclamatory question with pleonastic 'nicht' (French: ne explétif): 'How powerful is your magical sound!'

lines.original: weil holde Flöte durch dein Spielen
lines.literal: because, gracious flute, through your playing
even wild beasts joy feel.
lines.grammarNote: Subordinate clause verb-final placement: 'Freude fühlen'.

lines.literal: Yet only Pamina remains [absent] therefrom.
Pamina! Pamina! Hear, hear me! –
In vain, in vain! –

lines.original: Wo? wo? wo? ach wo, wo find' ich dich? –
lines.literal: Where? Where? Where? Ah where, where find I you? –

cues.speaker: Tamino
cues.stageDirectionTranslation: Papageno replies with his little panpipe.

lines.literal: Ha, that is Papageno's tone! –
Perhaps saw he Pamina already! –

lines.original: Vielleicht eilt sie mit ihm zu mir! –
lines.literal: Perhaps hurries she with him to me! –

lines.original: Vielleicht führt mich der Ton zu ihr!
lines.literal: Perhaps leads me the tone to her!

tokens.meaning: leads me the tone (V2 inversion: verb - object - subject)

lines.literal: Swift feet, quick courage,

lines.original: schützt vor Feindes List und Wut.
lines.literal: protects against enemy's cunning and fury.
Found we Tamino only [if only we found Tamino],

tokens.meaning: would we find / if we found (subjunctive II inversion)

lines.grammarNote: Optative wish inversion: 'Fänden wir ... doch' = If only we could find...

lines.literal: otherwise catch they us yet [or they will catch us]!
Lovely youth! –
Quiet, quiet, I can it better! –

cues.speaker: Papageno
cues.stageDirection: Papageno pfeift. Tamino antwortet von innen auf seiner Flöte.
cues.stageDirectionTranslation: Papageno whistles. Tamino replies from offstage on his flute.

lines.literal: Which joy is indeed greater,
Friend Tamino hears us already,
hither came the flute-tone.

lines.original: Welch ein Glück, wenn ich ihn finde,
lines.literal: What a fortune, if I him find,
only quickly, only quickly!
Only quickly, only quickly...

lines.original: Ha! – hab' ich euch noch erwischt!
lines.literal: Ha! – Have I you after all caught!

lines.original: Nur herbei mit Stahl und Eisen;
lines.literal: Only hither with steel and iron;

lines.original: wart, man wird euch Mores weisen!
lines.literal: wait, one will to-you manners show [we'll teach you manners]!

tokens.meaning: to teach someone manners / discipline (Latin mores)

lines.grammarNote: Idiom: 'jemandem Mores lehren/weisen' = to teach someone manners / discipline someone.

lines.literal: The Monostatos beguile [beguile Monostatos, will you]! –

lines.original: Nun herbei mit Band und Stricken,
lines.literal: Now hither with ties and ropes,
hey, you slaves come hither! –

lines.original: Ach! nun ist's mit uns vorbei!
lines.literal: Ah! Now is it with us over [it is all over for us]!
lines.grammarNote: Idiom: 'es ist mit jemandem vorbei' = it's all over for someone.

lines.literal: Hey! You slaves come hither!

lines.original: Wer viel wagt, gewinnt oft viel!
lines.literal: Who much ventures, wins often much!
lines.grammarNote: Proverbial relative clause: 'Wer viel wagt, gewinnt oft viel' (Nothing ventured, nothing gained).

lines.literal: Come, you beautiful chime-play [magic bells],
let the little-bells ring, ring,
so-that the ears to-them sing [their ears ring].
lines.grammarNote: German idiom: 'jemandem singen/klingen die Ohren' = someone's ears are ringing.

lines.original: Das klinget so herrlich, das klinget so schön!
lines.literal: That chimes so gloriously, that chimes so beautifully!

lines.original: La ra la la la la ra la la la la ra la.
lines.literal: La ra la la la la ra la la la la ra la.

lines.original: Nie hab' ich so etwas gehört und geseh'n!
lines.literal: Never have I such a-thing heard and seen!
lines.grammarNote: Fronted negative adverb 'Nie' triggers V2 inversion: 'hab' ich... gehört'.

lines.original: La ra la la la la ra la la la la ra la.
lines.literal: La ra la la la la ra la la la la ra la.
Could every upright man
lines.grammarNote: Hypothetical condition with verb-first syntax ('Könnte jeder...').

lines.literal: such little-bells find,
his enemies would then
without effort vanish.
And he would-live without them
in the best harmony!
Only friendship's harmony
mitigates the burdens,
without this sympathy [fellow-feeling],

tokens.meaning: mutual affinity / sympathy (in the Greek sense: feeling together)

lines.literal: is no happiness on earth.

tokens.meaning: on earth (archaic dative singular ending in -n)

lines.grammarNote: Archaic weak dative ending: 'auf Erden' for modern 'auf der Erde'.

lines.literal: Long live Sarastro! Sarastro long-live! –
lines.grammarNote: Third person subjunctive I optative: 'Es lebe...' = Long live...!

lines.original: Was soll dies bedeuten? Ich zitt're, ich bebe! –
lines.literal: What shall this mean? I tremble, I quake! –

lines.original: O Freund! nun ist's um uns getan!
lines.literal: O friend! Now is it about us done [we are done for]!

tokens.meaning: all over for us / done for

lines.grammarNote: German idiom: 'es ist um jemanden getan' = someone is finished / doomed.

lines.literal: This announces [the arrival of] Sarastro!

tokens.meaning: Sarastro (accusative with definite article in colloquial/regional German)

lines.grammarNote: Use of definite article with proper name ('den Sarastro') common in southern German/Austrian speech.

lines.literal: O were I a mouse,
how would I myself hide,

lines.original: wär' ich so klein wie Schnecken,
lines.literal: were I as small as snails,

lines.original: so kröch' ich in mein Haus! –
lines.literal: so would-creep I into my house [shell]! –

tokens.meaning: would creep / crawl (subjunctive II of kriechen)

lines.original: Mein Kind, was werden wir nun sprechen? –
lines.literal: My child, what will we now say? –

lines.original: Die Wahrheit – die Wahrheit, sei sie auch Verbrechen! –
lines.literal: The truth – the truth, be it even a crime! –

tokens.meaning: even though it be / even if it were (concessive subjunctive I)

lines.grammarNote: Concessive inversion: 'sei sie auch...' = even if it be...

cues.speaker: Pamina
cues.stageDirection: Ein Zug von Gefolge; zuletzt fährt Sarastro auf einem Triumphwagen heraus, der von sechs Löwen gezogen wird.
cues.stageDirectionTranslation: A procession of attendants enters; finally Sarastro arrives on a triumphal chariot drawn by six lions.

lines.original: Es lebe Sarastro, Sarastro soll leben!
lines.literal: Long live Sarastro, Sarastro shall live!

tokens.meaning: shall live / long life to him

lines.original: Er ist es, dem wir uns mit Freuden ergeben!
lines.literal: He is it, to-whom we ourselves with joy surrender!

lines.original: Stets mög' er des Lebens als Weiser sich freu'n. –
lines.literal: Always may he of-life as a sage rejoice. –

lines.original: Er ist unser Abgott, dem alle sich weih'n.
lines.literal: He is our idol, to-whom all themselves consecrate.
Lord, I am admittedly a-transgressor! –
I wanted from-your power to-flee. –
lines.grammarNote: 'Entfliehen' governs the dative of separation ('deiner Macht').

lines.original: Allein die Schuld ist nicht an mir!
lines.literal: Yet the fault is not on me [I am not to blame]!
The wicked Moor demanded love,

lines.original: darum, o Herr, entfloh ich dir! –
lines.literal: therefore, o Lord, fled I from-you! –

tokens.meaning: fled I from you (inversion with dative 'dir')

lines.original: Steh auf, erheit're dich, o Liebe,
lines.literal: Stand up, cheer yourself, o beloved,

lines.original: denn ohne erst in dich zu dringen,
lines.literal: for without first into you to press [without pressing you for answers],

tokens.meaning: without pressing / prying into (infinitive with zu)

lines.grammarNote: Prepositional infinitive clause: 'ohne ... zu + Infinitiv'.

lines.original: weiß ich von deinem Herzen mehr,
lines.literal: know I of your heart more,
you love another very-much.

lines.original: Zur Liebe will ich dich nicht zwingen,
lines.literal: To love will I you not force,
lines.grammarNote: Topicalized prepositional phrase triggering V2 inversion ('will ich dich...').

lines.original: doch geb' ich dir die Freiheit nicht.
lines.literal: yet give I to-you freedom not [yet I do not grant you freedom].
Me calls indeed filial-duty,

tokens.meaning: filial duty / duty of a child (Kind + Pflicht)

lines.grammarNote: OVS inversion: object 'Mich' fronted for rhetorical urgency.

lines.literal: for my mother –
stands in my power,

lines.original: du würdest um dein Glück gebracht,
lines.literal: you would-be of your happiness deprived,

tokens.notes: Passive subjunctive II: 'würdest um dein Glück gebracht' = would be cheated of your happiness.

lines.grammarNote: Idiom: 'jemanden um etwas bringen' = to rob / deprive someone of something.

lines.original: wenn ich dich ihren Händen ließe. –
lines.literal: if I you to-her hands left. –
lines.grammarNote: Conditional clause with 'wenn': verb 'ließe' at clause end.

lines.original: Mir klingt der Mutter Namen süße.
lines.literal: To-me sounds the mother's name sweet.

tokens.meaning: the mother's name (weak masculine noun 'Name' with -n in nominative/accusative in older German)

lines.original: Sie ist es – sie ist es –
lines.literal: She is it – she is it –
and a proud woman. –

lines.original: Ein Mann muß eure Herzen leiten,
lines.literal: A man must your hearts guide,

lines.original: denn ohne ihn pflegt jedes Weib
lines.literal: for without him is-accustomed every woman

tokens.meaning: is accustomed / tends to (pflegen + zu + Inf.)

lines.grammarNote: Construction: 'pflegen zu + Infinitiv' = to tend to / be in the habit of doing.

lines.literal: out-of her sphere-of-activity to step.

tokens.meaning: out of her sphere of influence (dative masculine)

lines.literal: Now, proud youth; just hither!
Here is Sarastro, our Lord! –
He is it,
She is it,
I believe it scarcely,
she is it,
he is it.
it is no dream.

lines.original: Es schling' mein Arm sich um ihn/sie her,
lines.literal: May entwine my arm itself around him/her round,
lines.grammarNote: Subjunctive I optative: 'Es schling' mein Arm sich...' = May my arm entwine around...

lines.original: und wenn es auch mein Ende wär'!
lines.literal: and even if it also my end were!
What shall that mean [what does this mean]?

tokens.meaning: what is the meaning of this

lines.literal: What an audacity!

lines.original: Gleich auseinander, das geht zu weit!
lines.literal: Immediately apart, that goes too far!

lines.original: Dein Sklave liegt zu deinen Füßen,
lines.literal: Your slave lies at your feet,
let the audacious transgressor atone.

lines.original: Bedenk, wie frech der Knabe ist!
lines.literal: Consider, how brazen the boy is!
lines.grammarNote: Indirect exclamation: verb 'ist' at the end.

lines.literal: Through this rare bird's cunning
wanted he Pamina from-you to-abduct,
lines.grammarNote: Dativus incommodi: 'dir entführen' = to kidnap away from you.

lines.literal: yet, I knew [how] him to-track-down.

tokens.meaning: to track down / detect (separable infinitive with zu)

lines.literal: You know me! – my vigilance –

lines.original: verdient, daß man ihr Lorbeer streut!
lines.literal: deserves, that one for-it laurel strews [scatters laurel before it]!
Hey! Give to-the man-of-honor immediately –

lines.original: Schon deine Gnade macht mich reich! –
lines.literal: Already your grace makes me rich! –
only seven and seventy bastinado-strokes [blows to the soles of the feet].

tokens.meaning: strokes on the soles of the feet (bastinado punishment)

lines.grammarNote: Historical corporal punishment: bastinado (blows with a rod across the bare soles of the feet).

lines.original: Ach Herr, den Lohn verhofft' ich nicht.
lines.literal: Ah Lord, that reward hoped-for I not.
lines.grammarNote: Fronted object 'den Lohn' triggering inversion: 'verhofft' ich nicht'.

lines.original: Nicht Dank! Es ist ja meine Pflicht!
lines.literal: No thanks! It is indeed my duty!

lines.original: Es lebe Sarastro, der göttliche Weise,
lines.literal: Long live Sarastro, the divine sage,

lines.original: er lohnet, und strafet in ähnlichem Kreise.
lines.literal: he rewards, and punishes in similar measure [equitably].

tokens.meaning: with equal justice / in like proportion

lines.literal: Lead these two strangers
into our trial-temple in [admit them],
cover their heads then –
lines.grammarNote: Masonic ritual: initiates have their heads veiled prior to the trials.

lines.literal: they must first purified be.

cues.speaker: Sarastro
cues.stageDirection: Zwei bringen eine Art Sack und bedecken die Häupter der beiden Fremden.
cues.stageDirectionTranslation: Two attendants bring cloths and veil the heads of the two strangers.

lines.literal: When virtue and justice

lines.original: den Großen Pfad mit Ruhm bestreu'n,
lines.literal: the great path with glory strew,
lines.grammarNote: Subordinate clause with 'wenn': verb 'bestreu'n' at the end.

lines.original: dann ist die Erd' ein Himmelreich,
lines.literal: then is the earth a heavenly-kingdom,
lines.grammarNote: Inversion after initial conditional result adverb 'dann': 'dann ist die Erd'...'.

lines.literal: and mortals to-the gods equal.
lines.grammarNote: 'Gleich' governs the dative ('den Göttern gleich' = equal to the gods).
